text:
maya: FYI — scheduling a proactive rolling reboot for us-central GPU racks (rack-c1, rack-c2, rack-c3) tonight 03:00-05:00 UTC. Reason: switch-management firmware update + thermal sensor recalibration. This is preemptive to avoid the noisy-neighbor latency spikes we've observed on chat/model endpoints.

sam: What impact on hosted pools? Any tenants pinned to those racks?

maya: Expected: short-term 8-12% reduction in available GPU capacity in us-central during the window while we drain. We'll drain workloads from affected nodes and route new requests to dedicated pools + the us-east hot spare. Enterprise tenants with pinned allocations will be routed to their fallback pools; no app-side config changes required.

priya: Can we canary on rack-c1 first and validate KV cache warmup? Last time a cold KV miss caused ~120ms p95 blips.

maya: Yes — plan is canary on rack-c1 (03:00-03:30), then rack-c2 (03:30-04:15), then rack-c3 (04:15-05:00). We'll pre-seed prefix/KV caches with the `kv-seed` job before returning capacity. Ops runbook snippet: `fleet cordon --rack=rack-c1 && fleet drain --grace=60`.

luca: Do we pause spot backfill during this window? Spot evictions + drain churn could amplify disruption.

maya: We'll disable spot backfill on affected pools for the duration. Also bump batching window for low-priority workloads +50% to reduce token churn and keep unit costs reasonable while capacity is reduced.

sam: @maya what about networking — any switch fabric reconfig or BGP flaps expected?

maya: It's a management-plane firmware update only; data-plane should be unaffected. Network verified BGP session retention in staging. We still have a network rollback plan if neighbor routes flap.

ops-bot: Scheduled: rack-c1 drain requested at 6111112222 — notifying oncall and updating maintenance ticket.

priya: :thumbsup: I'll watch p95 on /chat-models and the KV hit-rate dashboard. If p95 > 200ms for >3min we rollback.

luca: Cost note: disabling spot backfill + reserved failover traffic increases burn by ~$12/hr for the affected pools; estimated total ~$36 for the window. Acceptable tradeoff?

maya: Yes, product agreed — prioritizing latency stability for enterprise SLAs.

sam: No objections. Recommend we log perf deltas and attach to the maintenance ticket so the PMs can correlate with customer telemetry.

priya: I'll be oncall for the canary window; sam will take the rest.

maya: Thanks. I'll run a dry-run in staging at 01:00 UTC to validate cordon/drain scripts and the kv-seed job. Runbook and checklists: https://wiki.redwood/ops/maintenance/us-central-reboot-6111112222

ops-bot: Reminder: set PagerDuty escalation to 'maintenance' for services: inference-gateway, kv-cache, routing-service.

luca: Also watch cross-region routing for EU customers — if we shift traffic to us-east, end-to-end latency may increase; add an alert for cross-region failover rate.

maya: Good call. I'll add an alert for >5% cross-region fallback rate. Will post a 'starting' message 30m before the first canary and a final 'complete' when all racks are back in normal state.

sam: Thanks — everyone please ack when you can.

priya: ack

luca: ack

maya: ack — proceeding with comms and staging dry-run.
